explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/648: g(n) is the largest t such that there are integers 2 ≤ a_1 < ⋯ < a_t < n with P(a_1) > ⋯ > P(a_t), P the greatest prime factor; 'Estimate g(n)'. Cambie proved g(n) ≍ (n/log n)^{1/2}. In Lean g n is the supremum of t admitting a strictly increasing a : Fin t → ℕ with values in [2, n) and strictly decreasing Nat.maxPrimeFac (a bounded set, so a true maximum), and the statement is (n ↦ g n) =Θ[atTop] (n ↦ √(n/log n)), exactly Cambie's estimate. Faithful.
